comments.author: 1vuio0pswjnm7
comments.story: They Bypass YouTube Video Download Throttling
comments.text: The post-data OP is sending is different. In the script I shared it is easy to test one post-body against another, or one key against another, and so on. Most folks seem to using an "ANDROID" client, not "WEB". In the example I use "IOS" client but it does not matter. There are many clients that will work. To get throttled videoplayback URLs with the "WEB" client like the OP is using, one does not need to make POST requests to /youtubei/v1/player. There are throttled videoplayback URLs in the HTML of the /watch?v= page. For example, curl -A "" -40s [VIDEO] -o [LINK] -n 's/\\u0026/\&/g;/itag=22/p'

comments.author: 1vuio0pswjnm7
comments.story: They Bypass YouTube Video Download Throttling
comments.text: "However, acquiring this key decompiling the mobile application, monitoring requests through a proxy or relying on values discovered by others." This is again not true. The key is in the HTML of every /watch?v= YouTube page. It's a public key; it's not hidden in any way. Further, it's possible, up until today at least, to use the "WEB" key with clientName "ANDROID" of "IOS" and receive unthrottled URLs. The key in the shell script is in fact the WEB key. The key for IOS is different. curl -40s [VIDEO] \ |grep -o \"INNERTUBE_API_KEY...[^\"]*\"

comments.author: Kim_Bruning
comments.story: YouTube-dl has received a DMCA takedown from RIAA
comments.why: Creative Commons demo video suitable for multimedia tools.
comments.text: Lesson learned: always use Creative Commons licensed data to demo your multimedia tools. Else people get the wrong idea. Some examples for youtube-dl might be: * [VIDEO] Big buck bunny * [LINK] Sintel * [LINK] Spring In fact, youtube actually allows you to filter by CC, so there's never a reason not to!
